extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate students, faculty and higher-education leaders, administrators, program partners, and press/media
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational webpage describing AEI’s Academic Programs: mission, student and faculty programs (Summer/Winter Honors, Collegiate Network), resources, contacts, and multimedia/event recordings. Useful for prospective participants, faculty partners, and press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic Programs mission / purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The American Enterprise Institute’s Academic Programs team connects colleges and universities with the ideas and networks of AEI. We seek the renewal of healthy civic engagement on college campuses by facilitating educational and professional opportunities for students and faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All programs and resources for students and faculty advance ideas rooted in AEI’s belief in democracy, free enterprise, American strength and global leadership, solidarity with those at the periphery of our society, and a pluralistic, entrepreneurial culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student programs objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Our programs for students aim to provide the rising generation with the skills of civil and substantive discourse, strengthen their commitment to classical liberal ideas and institutions, and motivate them with AEI scholarship and the foundational principles that foster a competition of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While students come from a wide range of campuses and with varying public policy interests and ideological beliefs, they share a commitment to improving civic engagement on their campuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summer Honors Program eligibility & format
rubrics_metrics.description: The AEI Summer Honors Program is an intensive, fully-funded educational and professional development opportunity for top undergraduate students in Washington, DC centered on week-long seminars led by AEI scholars and distinguished civic leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key features: selective ('top undergraduate students'), fully-funded, intensive week-long seminars in Washington, DC led by AEI scholars and civic leaders. (Link: 'Learn More' for application details.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Collegiate Network purpose & audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The AEI Collegiate Network is an intellectual home for current undergraduates to engage with AEI scholarship, connect with AEI scholars, and cultivate relationships with other public-spirited students from campuses around the nation and world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended audience: current undergraduates seeking ongoing engagement with AEI; emphasizes networking with scholars and peers across campuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Winter Honors Program features
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2025, AEI’s Academic Programs is expanding its seminar offerings by launching a Winter Honors Program. This intensive, fully-funded educational and professional development opportunity will feature in-person and online seminars led by AEI scholars and partner instructors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights: expansion of seminar offerings, combination of in-person and online modalities, fully-funded, led by AEI scholars and partner instructors. (Link: 'Learn More' for program specifics.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty engagement network role & benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: AEI’s growing network of faculty and other higher education leaders is essential to our mission to renew healthy civic engagement on college campuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members help recruit students to AEI programs and facilitate events with AEI scholars on their campuses, as well as receive access to complimentary books and invitations to faculty-only gatherings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic Programs Marketing List eligibility & purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academic Programs Marketing List is available to students, faculty, administrators, and other partners of AEI’s Academic Programs from around the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: stay up-to-date on announcements and be the first to hear about unique, fully-funded programs for students and faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiative on Faith & Public Life resources
rubrics_metrics.description: From 2009-2021, the Initiative on Faith & Public Life ... produced a range of educational resources, including books, essays, videos, and documentaries. Today, many similar programs for students and faculty once offered through the initiative are made available directly with AEI’s Academic Programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: historical initiative materials and similar resources remain available via Academic Programs; useful for faith-oriented campus outreach and curricular resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event recordings and multimedia availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Event recordings and multimedia (panels, podcasts, summit recordings, discussions) are listed and available, covering topics such as intellectual diversity, civic education, and campus debates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed include Radcliffe in the Round, Collegiate Network Fall Summit recordings, podcasts and panels—resources for participants, faculty, and media to review past programming.
